notes:
1. Section 1 says "The idea is simple to say and hard to build". The sources (PYMNTS) say nothing about how hard it is to build. Fix: delete that sentence, or replace it with a plain restatement of the source, e.g. "World says the aim is to distinguish an AI agent connected to a verified human from anonymous automated traffic."
2. Dek says "World offers a way to tell agents tied to a verified person from anonymous traffic". Source: "the company said", "the release said" ("that offers a way to distinguish an AI agent connected to a verified human from anonymous automated traffic"). This is World's own claim stated as fact. Fix: "World says it offers a way to tell agents tied to a verified person from anonymous traffic". Apply the same attribution in section 1 if the sentence is kept.
3. Section 2 opens "Meanwhile Charles Schwab is preventing AI agents...". World's announcement was Sunday 18 Oct; Schwab's CEO spoke on the earnings call on Thursday 15 Oct (American Banker, published 15 Oct), so "Meanwhile" ties two events that were three days apart. Fix: "Charles Schwab is preventing AI agents..." or "Schwab said on its Thursday earnings call that it is preventing...".
4. Section 4 says "For those of us who run controls at a bank or lender, that is a good question to ask any vendor". This puts the author inside a bank's controls function (invented experience) and gives advice no source supports. Fix: make it pure argument with no claimed role, e.g. "Anyone checking an agent vendor can ask where the permission check happens and who can see it."
5. Section 4 says "OpenAI's report adds a caution from the builder's side". Nothing in the Fortune source calls the report a caution or OpenAI "the builder"; the report's own words are "This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder's permission". Fix: "OpenAI's report describes a different risk." or similar neutral wording.
